mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copy of passport / identity document of each non-resident shareholder (natural persons)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the country of origin or Spanish Consular Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Spain is a Contracting State under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); consular legalization required only for states outside the Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and register of directors/UBOs of the foreign corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry (e.g., Companies House, U.S. Secretary of State, German Handelsregister)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille + sworn official translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial Power of Attorney (POA) for incorporation formalities, name clearance, and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in country of origin or Spanish Consular Notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Apostille jurisdictions) + sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent credit institution in the shareholder's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank certificate + sworn Spanish translation (apostille not routinely required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory multi-layered screening under Art. 14 of Ley 10/2010 and SEPBLAC guidance: (i) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) identification covering foreign PEPs, domestic high-ranking officials, international organization officials, and their family members/close associates; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, and restrictive measures adopted by the Spanish Council of Ministers; (iii) adverse media/negative news check; (iv) beneficial-ownership verification at the 25% threshold (Art. 4.2 Ley 10/2010) before any banking relationship is established; enhanced due diligence (EDD) and mandatory refusal/termination duty where the UBO cannot be verified (Art. 4.3 Ley 10/2010).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – telematic certificate application at www.rmc.es, integrated with the CIRCE single incorporation window (www.circe.es) and the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad y Mercantiles de España network
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be drafted in Castilian Spanish or any co-official Spanish language (Art. 409 Reglamento del Registro Mercantil). Foreign-language denominators are admissible only when transliterated into Latin characters and phonetically adapted to Spanish, provided the resulting name is not misleading, is not identical or similar to an existing registered name, and complies with Art. 407 RRM. An SL must incorporate 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the abbreviation 'S.L.' (or 'S.L.U.' for single-member companies) as its legal-form indicator.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España / Estado / Nacional / Real / Oficial / expressions suggesting official public sponsorship (prior authorization by the Council of Ministers or competent administration required)
Banco / Caja / Financiera / Aseguradora / Seguros / Reaseguro / Mutua (financial and insurance tokens subject to prior Banco de España or DGSFP authorization)
Laboratorio / Farmacéutico / Sanidad / Clínica (pharma-sanitary tokens triggering prior clearance by the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices – AEMPS – and the Ministry of Health)
Sociedad Anónima / S.A. / S.A.U. (incompatible with the SL legal form)
Terms contrary to law, public order, or good customs; names liable to mislead as to the company legal form or actual activity (Art. 407.3 RRM)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social) must be delivered to the notary within 3 months (90 days) of issuance and is not renewable; upon expiry a fresh application is mandatory. If the Central Commercial Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file a reconsideration request (recurso de reposición) with the same Registrar within 15 business days, and thereafter an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice within 15 business days of the denial (Ley 39/2015, arts. 121–123). A substitute name may be filed immediately in parallel to avoid delaying the incorporation timeline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole physical seat for the GDP pharma freight operation. The SL must declare a registered office (domicilio social) situated in Spain (Art. 9 LSC) and, under Real Decreto 782/2013 and the EU Good Distribution Practice Guidelines (2013/C 343/01), must maintain a verifiable physical operational site with suitable warehousing, temperature-controlled storage capabilities, a responsible person / Qualified Person, and a documented pharmaceutical quality management system. A registered-service address (virtual office) may be used solely for correspondence and corporate notification purposes, but cannot substitute for the operational and tax domicile, which must be a real, accessible Spanish physical address subject to AEMPS inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High – >45% annual probability for GDP-licensed premises, because AEMPS and the competent autonomous health authorities perform mandatory pre-authorization on-site inspections and risk-based unannounced inspections under the national GDP inspection program, eudraGMDP protocols, and mutual-recognition/EMA audit exposure.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registrar tariff (arancel de los Registradores) scaled by capital, folios, and filings

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and/or consular legalization of foreign POA, identity documents, and parent-company registry records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent foreign authority (e.g., U.S. Secretary of State, UK FCDO, Spanish Consulate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule and apostille fees of the issuing sovereign authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation of foreign public and corporate documents (passport, POA, certificate of good standing, bank letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator / interpreter appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/CFT screening: PEP, OFAC SDN, UN, EU sanctions list check and UBO piercing investigation for all shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish law firm / licensed attorney (abogado colegiado)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for SL incorporations with cross-border UBO and pharma/GDP scope

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-10
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta de Constitución de la Sociedad Limitada
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of €3,000, fully paid up upon incorporation; no escrow account required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of ES Pharma Logistics SL, upon subscription of the entire share capital of €3,000 divided into 3,000 shares of €1 par value each, resolves unanimously as follows: (1) To adopt the registered office at Avenida de la Industria 456, 28001 Madrid, Spain; (2) To appoint Mr. Carlos Rodríguez as Managing Director and Ms. Ana García as Director; (3) To authorize the filing of the incorporation documents with the Registro Mercantil Central and the issuance of tax identification number; (4) To approve the initial corporate bylaws and appoint the first statutory auditor if applicable. This resolution is adopted in accordance with Article 8 of the LSRL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revision and re-submission if the notary identifies any formal defects

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Re-execution if any changes are required post-notarization

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Follow-up request if processing exceeds SLA

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agencia Española del Medicamento y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificado de Distribución de Medicamentos conforme a las Buenas Prácticas de Distribución (GDP)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Royal Decree 815/2013 on industrial emissions, wastewater discharge limits, and waste handling protocols

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections from local fire brigade and qualified engineer, plus workplace safety clearance from the Labor Authority (Inspección de Trabajo)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must first obtain an NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) through AEAT by submitting Form 036/030 and appointing a Spanish tax representative where applicable. Individual non-resident shareholders or administrators must obtain an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero). The SL obtains a provisional NIF at incorporation before a notary, and a definitive NIF after registration in the Mercantile Registry. For non-resident entities carrying on economic activity in Spain without a permanent establishment, VAT registration and NIF application must be filed with AEAT before the first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Spanish-resident SL is subject to Corporate Income Tax at 25% on worldwide income. Non-resident entities with a Spanish establishment are taxed on Spanish-source income. No pass-through election applies to an SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide a check-the-box election. Available elections include: (i) Group Tax Consolidation under Article 61 of the Spanish Corporate Income Tax Law for groups controlling at least 80% of a subsidiary; (ii) ETVE (Entidad de Tenencia de Valores Extranjeros) election for qualifying foreign-holding companies; (iii) specific depreciation and tax-credit options exercisable in the annual corporate tax return. EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive hybrid mismatch rules apply mandatorily, not by election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold; any economic activity performed in Spanish territory triggers mandatory VAT registration from the first taxable supply. For non-established suppliers of intra-EU distance sales of goods, an annual EUR 10,000 turnover threshold across the EU determines if Spanish VAT applies. Large taxpayers with annual turnover above EUR 6,018,121.97 are required to file SII periodic VAT information.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain mandates Verifactu-compliant electronic invoicing software for all businesses; B2B invoices must be generated in a format allowing integrity verification and legibility. Large taxpayers subject to SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) must submit invoice registers to AEAT via XML API in near real-time, generally within 4 calendar days (up to 8 days for monthly submitters). Invoices issued to Spanish public administrations must be submitted through the Face point using Facturae XML format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spain to a non-EU destination may be zero-rated (0% VAT) where the physical exit from the EU is proven within 90 days of supply and the exporter retains the evidence required by AEAT. Ancillary services directly connected to exported goods, including international transport, loading, handling, and GDP pharmaceutical freight services, may also qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is established outside Spain or the service is physically performed on exported goods. The exporter must demonstrate that title and risk passed and that the economic destination is outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DUA) with Export MRN
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR Transport Document
Inward Remittance Certificate / Bank proof of foreign receipt of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the zero-rating is applied without adequate export documentation, or where the goods are diverted improperly, AEAT may retroactively assess VAT at 21% plus late-interest penalties for up to 4 years. Penalties range from 50% to 150% of the undue tax benefit depending on intentionality and concealment. Knowingly false zero-rating claims may constitute criminal tax fraud under Articles 305-308 of the Spanish Criminal Code, attracting fines and imprisonment of up to 6 years. The exporter must retain all export and payment documents for at least 4 years and may be excluded from the export zero-rating register if repeat deficiencies are found.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under the Eurozone free current account convertibility regime pursuant to EU Regulation 2015/847 and Spanish Law 10/2010. Capital account transactions above €50,000 per transaction or €100,000 annually require prior notification to Banco de España. Profit remittance of dividends to non-resident shareholders is permitted after Spanish corporate tax and 19% withholding tax, subject to beneficial ownership identification via tax residency certificates and Form 210 filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds applies under Spanish law. Exporters must register operations with the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and file statistical declarations with Banco de España within 30 days for transactions exceeding €12,000. Foreign exchange receipts may be retained in international banking facilities without conversion ratios; all declarations must reference the original commercial invoice and proof of shipment.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. Spanish and EU regulations under MiCA and AMLD5 impose strict licensing and monitoring requirements; cross-border transfers must route exclusively through licensed Spanish or EU-authorized payment institutions with full KYC/AML compliance.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors and authorized signatories is mandatory for KYC interviews and execution of account opening documentation at Spanish branches. Remote digital onboarding is permitted only for existing customers via approved platforms; in-person verification remains standard for new Spanish SL corporate accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening failure or adverse media hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Director IDs, corporate charter, ownership structure chart, source of funds/wealth statements, and legal entity identifier verification

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or shell company indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized shareholder agreements, beneficial ownership declaration form, ultimate beneficial owner tax residency certificates, and Form 210 filings

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 'CAP' or 'EQTY'. Verification requires shareholder resolutions, bank statements, and tax filings (Form 210). All transactions must align with Spanish corporate law and Agencia Tributaria reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared via SWIFT MT103 for goods/services payments and Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600. For GDP pharma freight, use purpose codes 'GOODS' or 'SERVICES'. Settlements require export documentation and anti-money laundering transaction monitoring.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity optimization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Holding of the annual general meeting (Junta General) approving the annual accounts, with the approving resolution recorded in the corporate Minute Book.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting of the SL (internal corporate act; minutes retained in the statutory Minute Book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the first six (6) months after each fiscal year-end; for calendar-year SLs: on or before 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative fine for failure to hold the meeting, but directors incur civil liability toward shareholders and creditors and the delay makes the statutory 31 July registry deposit deadline impossible to meet, thereby triggering the Mercantile Registry sanctions set out below.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (Cuentas Anuales) — balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, notes, directors' report and audit report (when applicable), together with the certification of the shareholders' approval resolution and the annual UBO statement.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office; publication in the Official Gazette BORME.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month from the shareholders' meeting approval and no later than six (6) months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year SL: no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry economic fine of EUR 200 per month of delay, minimum EUR 1,200 and maximum EUR 60,000; repeated non-deposit triggers closure of the company's registry ledger sheet (cierre registral), blocking all new registrations of share transfers, director appointments and capital increases; the SL cannot obtain a good-standing certificate and persistent default may be considered in judicial dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return — Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), declaring taxable profit, withholdings, instalment payments made and applicable tax credits.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Madrid — electronic filing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: From 1 July through 25 July inclusive of the year following the close of the tax period for calendar-year taxpayers; in all cases within 25 days after the six-month period following the end of the tax period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% of the assessed amount depending on the delay bracket, plus statutory late-payment interest; minimum formal penalty EUR 200; substantial penalty of 50%–150% of the omitted amount for incorrect declarations; intentional non-filing with defrauded tax exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal tax offence.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ultimate beneficial owner declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real) — updated statement identifying every individual directly or indirectly holding more than 25% of share capital or ultimate control.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry, transmitted to SEPBLAC (Spanish financial intelligence unit).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually together with the deposit of annual accounts; calendar-year SL: by 31 July. Share transfers occurring during the year must be captured in the accompanying declaration or notified at the registry within ten (10) business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EUR 500 to EUR 1,500,000 under Ley 10/2010 depending on seriousness; the Mercantile Registry suspends inscription of share transfers and director appointments until the UBO statement is corrected; non-identified members may be denied dividend payments and voting rights.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legalization (certification) of the mandatory statutory corporate books — register of members, register of directors, minute book and accounting books — through the Mercantile Registry electronic legalization procedure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry ('legalización electrónica de libros').
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April of the year following the fiscal year to which the entries refer (within four (4) months after fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books lose probative evidentiary value before Spanish courts and tax authorities; legalization default generates a negative registry certificate impairing due-diligence acceptance by pharmaceutical GDP customers and weakening evidentiary support for accounting-based tax deductions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory when the SL exceeds, at both of two consecutive financial years, at least any two of the following thresholds: (a) total assets exceeding EUR 4,000,000; (b) annual net turnover exceeding EUR 8,000,000; (c) average workforce exceeding 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for parent companies of consolidated groups meeting the group-level thresholds and for listed, credit, insurance and other entities subject to special regulation under the Ley de Auditoría de Cuentas.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Chart of Accounts (Plan General de Contabilidad, Real Decreto 1514/2007) — national GAAP aligned with EU-IFRS; small and medium enterprises apply the PGC de PYMES (Real Decreto 1515/2007); micro-entities apply the micro-entity PGC; consolidated financial statements of EU-listed parent companies apply IFRS-EU. Annual accounts are prepared in Castilian Spanish and comprise the balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, notes and, where applicable, statement of cash flows.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL's administrator must file an updated Declaración de Titularidad Real at every annual deposit of annual accounts, making the UBO confirmation a recurring annual act rather than a one-off incorporation filing. The Mercantile Registry rejects share-transfer deeds and director appointments when the UBO statement is missing or inconsistent; identification data (full name, national ID, nationality, address and beneficial ownership percentage) must be provided for every individual holding over 25% of share capital or ultimate control, and any share transfer must be accompanied by the transferee's updated identification before the inscription is allowed.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Sole-shareholder contract book (Libro de Contratos con el Socio Único) — required only in single-member SL structures

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 2,400 per year (gestoría administrative compliance services, registered office representation and corporate secretarial support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,500 – USD 16,000 per certified audit engagement (market range for an SME-scale Spanish pharmaceutical logistics company)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly incorporated entities may apply a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory eligibility conditions. Qualifying small entities may benefit from reduced rates under applicable legislation. Research and development deductions, technological innovation deductions, patent-box reductions, employment incentives, and regional incentives may reduce the effective burden. The general participation exemption may exclude qualifying dividend and capital-gain income, normally subject to a 5% non-deductible expense adjustment. Spanish tax losses are generally carried forward without a statutory time limit, subject to utilization limitations; however, this dossier retains the mandated five-year schema value in the next field.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) Sede Electrónica. Modelo 202 is used for corporate income tax advance payments where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual for Modelo 200; quarterly advance payments for Modelo 202 in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within the first 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary filing window is 1 to 25 July, subject to the applicable electronic-filing and payment rules. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; large taxpayers may have additional payment and filing mechanics.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish tax identification number (NIF), legal name, registered office, tax period start and end dates, activity classification, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or parent does not replace the Spanish SL's NIF or tax period. Report the Spanish resident entity as the taxpayer and identify the non-resident owner only in related-party, withholding, ownership, or group-information fields.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the profit or loss before corporate income tax based on statutory accounts prepared under the Spanish General Accounting Plan.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's own statutory accounts. Do not substitute the parent company's consolidated profit, foreign branch results, or group management accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report permanent and temporary positive or negative adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, financial expense limitations, exempt income, and tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign parent costs unless they are legally attributable to the Spanish SL, properly invoiced, economically justified, and arm's-length. Apply withholding taxes and treaty exemptions separately from the Spanish taxable-profit computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose controlled transactions, valuation methods, counterparties, transaction categories, and amounts where required by Modelo 200 and related reporting rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with non-resident shareholders, group companies, financing entities, logistics providers, licensors, and service companies. Maintain contemporaneous Spanish transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter available tax-loss carryforwards, losses utilized in the period, and remaining balances. Utilization is subject to statutory percentage limitations and minimum taxable-income rules, particularly for larger taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses legally incurred by the Spanish SL or validly transferred under a qualifying Spanish tax-consolidation regime may be used. Foreign parent losses cannot be entered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the adjusted taxable base, applicable rate, gross tax liability, and any reduced-rate or incentive computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the Spanish resident-company rate and incentives, not the rate of the shareholder's jurisdiction. The 15% new-entity rate requires separate eligibility verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim documented deductions and credits for research and development, technological innovation, employment, investments, donations, double taxation, and other legally available items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent’s tax credit cannot normally be claimed by the Spanish SL. Spanish-source withholding or foreign-tax credits require statutory entitlement and supporting certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter Modelo 202 payments and other payments made against the annual liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all advance payments to the Spanish SL's tax identification number and tax period. Do not allocate parent-company instalments to the subsidiary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Withholding and payments on account received
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying Spanish withholding credits supported by withholding certificates and accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding suffered by a non-resident shareholder is not automatically a credit of the Spanish SL. Dividend, interest, royalty, and service withholding must be attributed to the legal recipient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the amount payable or refundable and select payment by bank debit, NRC, direct payment, or other authorized electronic method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use a Spanish-authorized payment route and maintain evidence of successful electronic submission, payment reference, and filing receipt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate advance payments either by applying the statutory percentage to the prior-period assessment or, where mandatory or elected, by applying the percentage to the current-period accounting base with statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must assess whether turnover thresholds require the current-period-base method or other large-taxpayer rules. Foreign group turnover may be relevant to threshold analysis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no tax due generally attracts a fixed surcharge based on delay, commonly 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months and 15% thereafter, subject to statutory rules and reductions. Late payment normally attracts a surcharge ranging from 5% to 20%, depending on timing, with interest potentially applying after the statutory period. Incorrect or incomplete returns may incur administrative penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the underpaid amount, depending on concealment, repetition, and fraud-related factors. Electronic-filing failures may also trigger procedural penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, Pago fraccionado del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, filed electronically through AEAT Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly, ordinarily in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. Where payment by direct debit is used, an earlier bank-debit deadline may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Spanish SL's NIF, legal name, tax period, financial year, and applicable corporate-tax regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the Spanish SL as the taxpayer even where the economic owner is non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select bank debit, NRC, or another authorized electronic payment method and record the payment reference.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment account and authorization must satisfy Spanish AEAT and banking requirements; a foreign parent's account is not automatically acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the instalment by applying the statutory percentage to the prior-period corporate-tax liability, after permitted adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the calculation exclusively to the Spanish SL's prior Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Where mandatory or elected, calculate the instalment using current-period accounting profit through the relevant quarter, adjusted under corporate-tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Spanish SL income and deductible expenses. Related-party charges must be arm's-length and supported before inclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply statutory minimum-payment rules and special rates where the taxpayer's net turnover meets the relevant large-taxpayer thresholds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess group and prior-year turnover aggregation rules and obtain specialist confirmation before filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or payment may produce surcharges, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties. Underpayments may generate a penalty based on the unpaid amount, commonly 50% to 150% where the conduct is classified as an incorrect or fraudulent tax filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. Qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief may reduce withholding to 0% where ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse, beneficial-ownership, and other statutory conditions are satisfied. The Spanish payer must obtain and retain supporting documentation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid tax-residence certificate issued by its competent foreign tax authority, normally valid for the period accepted under Spanish administrative practice, together with beneficial-owner and treaty-entitlement evidence. The Spanish payer applies the domestic exemption or treaty rate only where the legal conditions and documentation are satisfied, retains the certificate and ownership evidence, and reports the payment through the applicable withholding return, generally Modelo 216, with annual information reporting through Modelo 296. If full relief is not applied at source, the recipient may generally seek a refund through the applicable non-resident tax procedure, subject to limitation periods and documentary requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Spanish domestic non-resident income tax rates are generally 19% for recipients resident in the EU or European Economic Area where statutory conditions apply and 24% for other non-residents; the exact rate depends on the income category and recipient jurisdiction. Under an applicable tax treaty, interest and royalties are commonly capped at treaty-specific rates, frequently 5%, 8%, 10%, or 15%, but the relevant treaty must be reviewed individually. Qualifying associated EU companies may obtain 0% withholding on interest and royalties under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive if ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, beneficial-ownership, and anti-abuse requirements are met. Spanish withholding generally applies to Spanish-source payments unless a valid exemption or treaty limitation is documented.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally not required for the aggregate controlled transactions of the same type with the same related person or entity when the amount does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length, subject to statutory exclusions. A Local File is otherwise generally required for material controlled transactions. Master File obligations generally apply to Spanish entities belonging to a group, subject to exemptions including qualifying small-entity cases; Spanish group documentation rules must be tested against the EUR 45 million net-turnover threshold and other statutory conditions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups meeting the EUR 750 million consolidated-revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate standalone Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore ESR regimes. Substance is nevertheless required in applying Spanish transfer-pricing rules, beneficial-ownership standards, the principal-purpose and anti-abuse rules, the general anti-avoidance rule, controlled foreign company rules, EU anti-abuse provisions, and the anti-conduit doctrine. A Spanish SL should maintain genuine local management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure proportionate to its functions, Spanish accounting and records, decision-making evidence, commercial risk assumption, and demonstrable GDP-compliant logistics activity. Pure conduit arrangements, circular cash flows, artificial royalty or interest deductions, and back-to-back transactions may be challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional concealment of revenue, fabricated expenses, false invoices, double accounting, sham logistics costs, deliberate understatement of taxable income, or use of undocumented cash transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and collection surcharges. Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 per tax and assessment period may constitute a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or organized and fraudulent conduct, may attract imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers who intentionally participate may incur criminal liability, civil restitution, fines, disqualification from public office or business management, and subsidiary civil liability. Travel restrictions or pre-trial detention are possible only under judicial order and are not automatic consequences of an assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length freight, management, financing, royalty, commission, or procurement charges; unsupported year-end true-ups; omission of related parties; or failure to maintain required Local File or Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make primary and secondary adjustments, deny deductions, recharacterize distributions, assess tax and interest, and impose specific documentation penalties. Related-party documentation breaches can generate fixed penalties per omitted, inaccurate, or false data item, subject to statutory minimums and maximums; deliberate underpayment can additionally attract percentage-based tax penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability where they cause or materially facilitate non-payment, concealment, or obstruction. Serious intentional conduct may also support criminal tax-fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend, interest, and royalty withholding failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying non-resident dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate, or misclassifying distributions as deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for the unwithheld tax, late-payment interest, and withholding penalties generally calculated as a percentage of the unpaid amount. The payer may lose access to exemption or treaty relief and may be required to file corrected withholding returns and annual information returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability for deliberate or negligent failure to withhold and may be liable for civil damages or criminal consequences where the conduct forms part of tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial substance, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL solely as a conduit, maintaining no real functions or risks, routing payments through an entity lacking beneficial ownership, circularly transferring funds, or claiming EU or treaty relief without commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may deny treaty or directive benefits, apply beneficial-ownership and anti-abuse doctrines, recharacterize transactions, impose withholding and corporate-tax assessments, and apply penalties and interest. The general anti-avoidance rule may apply where legally permitted steps are artificial or primarily tax-driven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally exposed for knowingly implementing abusive structures, including civil restitution, administrative fines, management disqualification, and criminal liability where tax-fraud thresholds or other offences are met.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting fictitious invoices, manipulating inventory or freight records, destroying accounting evidence, maintaining parallel books, or recording unsupported pharmaceutical logistics expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax penalties, accounting sanctions, assessment of omitted tax, interest, and possible criminal offences for document falsification or accounting fraud may apply. Serious falsification can lead to imprisonment and fines under the Spanish Criminal Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accountants, and operational managers may be personally liable where they ordered, approved, or knowingly used false records. Courts may impose imprisonment, fines, disqualification, and civil compensation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify customers or beneficial owners, inadequate risk assessment, unexplained cash or crypto flows, failure to retain records, failure to report suspicious transactions, or facilitating sanctions evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious infringements may attract substantial corporate fines, commonly up to the greater of statutory fixed amounts, percentages of annual turnover, or multiples of the unlawfully obtained benefit, together with public reprimand, authorization restrictions, or management disqualification. Exact sanctions depend on classification and applicable amendments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal fines, disqualification, civil liability, and criminal money-laundering liability. Imprisonment may apply to knowing participation; travel restrictions require judicial measures and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Pharmaceutical GDP and logistics licensing breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating pharmaceutical distribution or clinical-logistics activities without the required authorization, failing temperature-control and traceability requirements, using unqualified subcontractors, or handling medicinal products outside authorized channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish pharmaceutical and health authorities may impose administrative fines, suspend or revoke authorizations, order product withdrawal or destruction, and impose operational closure. Serious conduct may create civil liability for patient, product, or customer harm and may constitute a criminal offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible technical personnel may face personal administrative, civil, and criminal liability where they knowingly authorize unsafe, unauthorized, or falsified pharmaceutical handling.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Social-security, payroll, and worker misclassification fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting wages, concealing employees, misclassifying workers, failing to withhold payroll taxes, or using sham contractors for warehouse, transport, or compliance functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may owe unpaid social-security contributions, payroll taxes, interest, surcharges, and employment-law penalties. Fraudulent conduct may produce criminal liability where statutory thresholds are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may incur subsidiary liability for unpaid contributions and criminal liability for deliberate fraud, together with civil compensation and management disqualification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import VAT, and sanctions evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misclassification of pharmaceutical products, undervaluation, false origin claims, diversion of controlled goods, or dealings with sanctioned counterparties and jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs duties, import VAT, interest, seizure, forfeiture, administrative fines, and possible criminal penalties may apply. Sanctions breaches may result in severe fines and asset-freezing measures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may face civil and criminal liability, fines, disqualification, and judicial travel restrictions where they knowingly authorize or facilitate customs or sanctions offences.
